metaDescription: Six microwave splatter guards compared: collapsible silicone, glass, rigid plastic and tall vented covers, with notes on size, venting and cleanup.
introParagraphs: Anyone who has reheated a bowl of tomato soup knows how far a microwave can throw a meal. Sauce bubbles up, bursts against the ceiling and bakes onto the walls, and by the next day it takes a damp sponge and some patience to remove. A splatter guard is a vented cover that sits over the bowl or plate, holds the spray in and lets enough steam out that nothing boils over or turns the food rubbery.

The six guards in this guide cover the main designs. The Tovolo and the CasaCulina are collapsible silicone-style covers that pop up for tall dishes and flatten for storage. The Le'raze is made of borosilicate glass with a cool-touch handle. The Nordic Ware is a rigid clear plastic pair, the HIC Kitchen is a four-piece set of flat covers in two sizes, and the Tusjiain is a tall cover for deep bowls and big plates.

We evaluated each model from its listing, stated dimensions and materials, and repeated themes in buyer feedback, without claiming hands-on testing. The comparison asks whether a guard fits your dishes, vents steam well, tolerates the microwave, and cleans up without fuss. A guard that does not fit your usual plate or bowl will sit in the drawer, so fit is the first filter.

products.name: Tovolo Collapsible Microwave Splatter Cover
products.description:
The Tovolo cover is the one most people picture when they think of a modern collapsible microwave lid. It is a 10.5 inch medium silicone cover with a vented design that lets steam out, an easy-grip handle, and a charcoal color that hides stains better than a clear lid would. The listing says the materials are BPA-free and food safe, which is the baseline you want for something that touches hot food.

The collapsible shape is the point. A rigid cover is stuck at a fixed height, while a collapsible one can stand taller over a heaped plate and fold flat when it is in the drawer. The listing also notes that it doubles as a colander, which is a real second use for rinsing fruit or draining pasta in a pinch. That dual role is a good reason to prefer it over a flat plastic lid if drawer space is limited.

As with most silicone, be mindful that it can hold odors and a faint film from oily dishes, so wash it promptly. Compared with the Le'raze glass lid, it is lighter and easier to store but will not feel as rigid. Compared with the CasaCulina, it is a single cover instead of a pair. For a general-purpose household cover, it is the safest all-round choice.
products.bestFor: A one-cover household that wants a collapsible, easy-to-store design.
cons: Silicone can hold odors from oily food

products.name: Le'raze 10 Inch Glass Microwave Splatter Cover

specList.label: Venting
specList.value: Dual vent holes, side and top

products.description:
The Le'raze guard is a pure glass cover rather than plastic or rubber. The listing describes it as borosilicate glass, which it says will not melt, scratch or fade, and which is a cleaner-feeling choice for anyone who prefers to avoid plastic touching hot food. It has an easy-grip, cool-touch handle and is listed as dishwasher safe, lead-free and BPA-free.

Venting is handled by a dual hole system, one on the side and one on top. The idea is to let steam escape in a controlled way so the food heats evenly without a pressure build-up under the lid. Glass also lets you see the food, so you can watch for bubbling at the edge instead of lifting the lid and releasing the heat.

The tradeoffs are weight and fragility. Glass is heavier than silicone, can chip or crack if knocked against a counter, and does not collapse for storage. At 10 inches it fits a typical dinner plate or a medium bowl but not an extra-large dish. Compared with the Tovolo, it gives you a rigid, see-through lid with no odor retention. If you reheat often and like a sturdy cover, it is the premium choice.
products.bestFor: Cooks who prefer a rigid, see-through glass cover that goes in the dishwasher.
pros: Borosilicate glass will not melt or fade
Dual vent holes on side and top

products.name: CasaCulina Collapsible Microwave Splatter Cover 2 Pack

specList.label: Height
specList.value: Pops up to 3.2 inches, folds to 1.2 inches

products.description:
The CasaCulina set gives you two collapsible covers, one red and one grey, so you can reheat two dishes at the same time or keep a spare in the drawer. The listing states a perforated top that lets steam out, a lid that pops up to 3.2 inches to cover tall dishes and piles of food, and a folded height of 1.2 inches. Those numbers are useful because they tell you exactly how much room it takes in a cabinet.

The ergonomic handle on each pop-up lid makes it easy to lift the cover out of a hot microwave, and the listing also mentions a hook hole for hanging. The two-cover pack is where the value is: most households eventually need one cover for a plate and another for a bowl, and having a pair stops you from washing between uses.

The flip side is that pop-up covers are never as tall as the Tusjiain, and the flexible material may flop under the heat of a long cook. Compared with the Tovolo, you get more covers for a similar shape; compared with the HIC set, you get a taller dome. If you cook for two or heat leftovers often, the pair is the practical choice.
products.bestFor: Households that reheat two dishes at a time and want covers that fold flat.
pros: Pops up to 3.2 inches for tall food
cons: Not as tall as a rigid dome
Flexible lid can sag when hot
Two colors may not suit all kitchens

products.name: Tusjiain Tall Large Microwave Splatter Cover
products.description:
If your usual reheating involves a deep bowl of chili or a plate piled with pasta, the Tusjiain is the cover with the most headroom. The listing gives dimensions of about 11.5 by 11.5 by 4.5 inches, which is the tallest and widest of the covers in this guide. That depth gives food room to bubble without touching the lid, and a wider footprint means a big plate will not leave edges exposed.

The maker describes enlarged perforated steam vents to release moisture and discourage condensation, along with a grip handle shaped for the hand. The goal is to keep the microwave clean while letting vapor out, which also tends to speed up heating a little because steam is not trapped over the food. A tall cover is also less likely to knock into a spoon sticking out of a bowl.

Size is the cost. A tall 11.5 inch cover takes more storage room than the collapsible options, and it may not fit a small microwave with a low ceiling. Compared with the Tovolo, it offers more clearance but does not fold. Compared with the Le'raze glass lid, it is lighter and less fragile. For deep dishes, this is the one to buy.
products.bestFor: Deep bowls, big plates and heaped portions that need headroom.
pros: Tallest cover in the guide at 4.5 inches

products.name: Nordic Ware Microwave Splatter Cover Set of 2
products.description:
Nordic Ware's cover is the traditional rigid design: a clear plastic dome with a slight dip in the top and a lip that rests on the plate. The listing gives a 10.4 inch interior diameter at the lip and a 10.5 inch exterior diameter, and the set contains two covers. It is made from BPA-free and melamine-free plastic and is listed as top rack dishwasher safe.

Because the plastic is clear, you can see the food without lifting the lid, and the shape keeps splatter in while the maker says it also keeps food warm after cooking. Rigid covers are easy to stack and do not droop, which suits an older drawer or a tidy cabinet. They tend to last for years because there are no hinges or flexible folds to wear out.

The tradeoff is that plastic covers can stain and cloud with tomato-based foods and must go on the top rack of a dishwasher. They also do not collapse, so storage space is a consideration. Compared with the CasaCulina pair, the Nordic Ware set is sturdier but bulkier. If you want a plain, dependable pair with no moving parts, this is the one.
products.bestFor: Simple, durable covers that stack in the cabinet and show the food.
pros: Clear plastic lets you watch the food
cons: Top rack only in the dishwasher

products.name: HIC Kitchen Microwave Splatter Guards Set of 4

specList.label: Sizes
specList.value: 2 small 5 x 5 inch, 2 large 9 x 9 inch

products.description:
The HIC Kitchen set takes a different approach: four small flat guards instead of one big dome. The listing says there are two small 5 by 5 inch covers and two large 9 by 9 inch covers, made from food-safe BPA-free plastic rated heat safe to 212 degrees Fahrenheit. A textured surface vents steam to help control moisture, and the guards are meant for bowls, containers and deep dishes.

Four pieces mean flexibility. The small guards suit a mug or a ramekin, the large ones fit a bowl or a container, and you can use two at once. They are also easy to store because they are thin and flat. The listed 212 degree limit is worth respecting, so use them for reheating and short cooks, not for long, dry heating.

Because these are flat covers, they sit on the dish instead of standing above it. That means they are less suited to heaped plates than the Tusjiain or the CasaCulina. Compared with the Nordic Ware dome, the HIC set is more adaptable but offers less headroom. If you reheat in many different containers, it is the most flexible option.
products.bestFor: Cooks who reheat in mugs, bowls and containers of different sizes.
cons: Low heat rating limits long cooks

buyingCriteria.explanation: A cover that is smaller than the dish just sits inside it or leaves the edges exposed. Measure the plates and bowls you reheat most and choose a cover a little larger than the rim. The Le'raze is 10 inches, the Tovolo is 10.5 inches, and the Tusjiain is about 11.5 inches, so a dinner plate of 10 to 11 inches is covered by any of them. The HIC large guards are 9 by 9 inches, so they suit bowls and containers, not full plates.

Food that bubbles, like soup or sauce, needs space between the surface and the lid. If it touches the cover it can leak out through the vents. The Tusjiain stands about 4.5 inches tall, the CasaCulina pops up to 3.2 inches, and the HIC guards sit flat. Pick the tallest option that still fits your microwave and your usual dishes.

A good cover must vent steam, because a sealed lid can build pressure and make the cover pop or the food cook unevenly. Look for perforations on top, as in the CasaCulina and Tusjiain, or side and top holes as on the Le'raze. The HIC set uses a textured surface to vent. Stir the food partway through cooking, and lift the cover away from your face to avoid a steam burn.

Glass, silicone and plastic all behave differently. Glass such as the Le'raze will not scratch or fade but can break, while silicone such as the Tovolo collapses and holds up well but can hold odors. The HIC plastic covers are rated heat safe to 212 degrees Fahrenheit, which is fine for reheating but not for long dry cooks. Always check the temperature limit on the product page.

Tomato sauce stains many plastics, and oily food leaves a film on silicone. Glass is the easiest to clean thoroughly, and the Le'raze and Nordic Ware are listed as dishwasher safe, with the Nordic Ware on the top rack only. Rinse covers soon after use, because dried sauce is harder to remove. Check whether the maker recommends hand washing.

A cover you cannot store easily tends to live on the counter. Collapsible options like the Tovolo and CasaCulina fold flat, while the Tusjiain and Nordic Ware domes take more space. The HIC pieces are thin and stack neatly. A good handle also matters, because lifting a hot lid is where burns happen. Choose a handle you can grip with a mitt.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fit and height
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated diameters and heights to common plates and bowls. The Tusjiain leads on headroom with about 4.5 inches, and the CasaCulina offers a pop-up height of 3.2 inches. Flat guards like the HIC were credited for their small size but less for tall dishes.

howWeEvaluated.title: Steam venting
howWeEvaluated.description: Each cover was assessed for how it releases moisture and prevents pressure build-up. Dual hole venting on the Le'raze, perforated tops on the CasaCulina and Tusjiain, and the textured HIC surface were compared. Covers with no clear venting description were scored cautiously.

howWeEvaluated.title: Material and heat limits
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at whether the listing names glass, silicone or plastic and whether it gives a temperature limit. The HIC lists 212 degrees Fahrenheit, while the Le'raze listing says its borosilicate glass will not melt or fade. A stated limit earned more credit than a vague claim, and a missing one earned less.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cleaning and upkeep
howWeEvaluated.description: Dishwasher safety and staining behavior were weighed. The Le'raze and Nordic Ware are listed as dishwasher safe, and silicone covers can hold odors. Easy cleaning matters because microwave covers see grease and sauce daily.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lineup positioning
howWeEvaluated.description: Within this group, the Tusjiain leads on height, the Le'raze on material, the CasaCulina on pairing and fold height, the HIC on variety, the Nordic Ware on simplicity and the Tovolo on all-round versatility. We framed badges around these differences rather than a single ranking.

faq.q: Do microwave splatter guards need vent holes?
faq.a: Yes. Steam has to escape or pressure builds under the cover and can push food out or make the cover pop up. Look for perforations on top or vents on the side, like those on the CasaCulina and Le'raze. Stir the food partway through cooking and lift the cover away from your face.

faq.q: Can I use a splatter guard instead of plastic wrap?
faq.a: In most cases yes, and it is easier because you can reuse it. A vented cover also avoids the risk of plastic wrap touching hot food. Make sure the cover is rated for microwave use and keep the vents clear. Use a larger guard for tall dishes.

faq.q: How do I get tomato stains out of a plastic cover?
faq.a: Wash promptly with warm soapy water, and for stains, try a paste of baking soda and water left on for a while. Glass covers like the Le'raze do not stain in the same way. Sunlight can also fade surface stains on plastic. Avoid abrasive pads that scratch the plastic.

faq.q: Is a collapsible cover safe in the microwave?
faq.a: Look for one that states food-safe, BPA-free silicone and check the listed temperature limit. The Tovolo and CasaCulina are meant for microwave use. Do not use them for dry heating, and keep them away from heating elements in combination ovens.

faq.q: What size cover do I need?
faq.a: Pick a cover slightly larger than the rim of your biggest dish. A 10 inch cover works for most plates, while an 11 inch cover like the Tusjiain covers larger ones. If you reheat in mugs and small bowls, the small HIC guards fit better. Measure your microwave height too.

faq.q: Can glass covers crack in the microwave?
faq.a: Borosilicate glass, as in the Le'raze listing, handles heat well, but any glass can break from impact or a sudden temperature change. Let it cool before rinsing it with cold water. Check for chips before each use and replace it if damaged.
